source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirty healthy white guinea pigs of mixed sexes were used in this study.
source_quotes.randomised: Animals were randomly divided into a normal control group (n=10) and a gentamicin cochlear poisoning group (n=20).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The waveform of the signal was a sinusoidally enveloped random phase pip of 32.5 kHz and 85.0 kHz in 0.5 ms duration.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: The waveform of the signal was a sinusoidally enveloped random phase pip of 32.5 kHz and 85.0 kHz in 0.5 ms duration.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Induction was performed using clicks, 30–35 kHz pulse square wave (pulse frequency was 100 times/s) and 80–90 kHz pulse square wave (pulse frequency was 100 times/s).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Induced parameters were TR2000 and TE20, with 600 repetitions, 20 min scanning time, acoustic stimulation for 20 s, and no acoustic stimulation for 10 s.

flags.reason: Stimulus intensity was reported only as amplifier output peak-to-peak voltage relative to a 20 V (0 dB) reference; no pressure (kPa) or intensity (W/cm2) value was given.
Paper does not discuss adverse events or safety of the ultrasound stimulation itself (only gentamicin-induced cochlear damage, which is the disease model, not an ultrasound safety outcome).
This study is itself about perception of ultrasound via the cochlea; the standard 'auditory confound' vocabulary does not map cleanly, so left not_reported.

readout_other: auditory brainstem response (ABR) threshold; BOLD fMRI region-of-interest (ROI) induced by bone-conducted ultrasound; immunofluorescence for Prestin, Otoferlin and F-Actin in cochlear hair cells
direction_notes: Bone-conducted ultrasound induced ABR responses and cerebral cortex BOLD ROI in normal guinea pigs at both frequency bands, but in gentamicin-poisoned (cochlear hair-cell damaged) animals only the higher (80-90 kHz) frequency induced responses, while 30-35 kHz did not, indicating hair-cell involvement in low-frequency ultrasound perception.

exposures.label: Bone-conducted ultrasound to cochlea (30-35 kHz and 80-90 kHz)

target.label: bone-conducted ultrasound via the mastoid region (cochlea)

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasonic vibration was generated by a triggered function generator system and delivered through an ultrasonic transducer as a sinusoidally enveloped random-phase pip of 32.5 kHz and 85.0 kHz in 0.5 ms duration; for ABR, 30-35 kHz and 80-90 kHz pulse square waves were used (pulse frequency 100 times/s). For fMRI ROI detection, bone-conducted pulsed square waves were used with acoustic stimulation for 20 s and no acoustic stimulation for 10 s, over a 20-min scan (600 repetitions). Stimulus intensity was expressed as amplifier output peak-to-peak voltage (max 20 V = 0 dB reference), not as an absolute acoustic pressure or intensity.
